questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes You must answer on the multiple choice answer sheet. You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS • There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. • For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Write in soft pencil. • Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. • Do not use correction fluid. • Do not write on any bar codes. • You may use a calculator. INFORMATION • The total mark for this paper is 30. • Each correct answer will score one mark. • Any rough working should be done on this question paper.

The transport authority in a city is considering building an underground railway to reduce traffic congestion on the roads. Which combination would represent an external cost and an external benefit of the use of this railway? external cost external benefit

options.A: compensation is paid to businesses foreign tourists pay to use the railway displaced by construction work
options.B: nearby residents suffer there are fewer admissions to noise from passing trains hospital as air quality improves
options.C: overtime payments are made to workers productivity increases as employees to finish building the railway on time arrive at work more punctually
options.D: reduced traffic means there are motorists spend less on fuel fewer road improvements needed

questions.questionText: In which type of market structure are commercial banks usually found?

options.A: perfect competition, because they all link their interest rates to that of the central bank
options.B: perfect competition, because they offer identical products and services
options.C: monopolistic competition, because a competitive market prevents them making excess profits
options.D: oligopoly, because they are affected by the actions of other banks

questions.questionText: The manufacture of some sports equipment is dominated by very large firms but there are also smaller firms in the industry. What enables a small firm to exist in such an industry?

options.A: high concentration ratio that reduces competition
options.B: high start-up costs that occur in a contestable market
options.C: decreasing average cost as a large firm expands
options.D: a requirement for personalised equipment

questions.questionText: The marginal cost curve of a firm passes through the lowest point of the firm’s

options.A: average fixed cost curve.
options.B: average variable cost curve.
options.C: marginal revenue curve.
options.D: total cost curve.

questions.questionText: What would definitely be abnormal profits?

options.A: the extra revenue received from the sale of a farmer’s land to a house-building firm
options.B: the extra revenue received by a firm from an unexpectedly large increase in demand
options.C: the total revenue from the sale of a firm’s products in excess of the total variable costs of the firm
options.D: the total revenue in excess of total costs of the firm above the minimum needed to keep the firm in business in the long run

A government regards fresh fruit and vegetables as merit goods, and subsidises agriculture to boost their production. What could be a government failure arising from these subsidies?

options.A: cheaper fresh fruit and vegetables
options.B: land clearance reducing wildlife
options.C: lower spending on treating dietary illnesses
options.D: more jobs picking fruit and vegetables

questions.questionText: The table shows a firm that has four possible methods of production. Each method has a different cost and causes a different amount of pollution. The government decides that polluting firms must buy pollution permits that cost $90 each. Each permit allows the firm to emit 1 tonne of pollution. No pollution can be emitted without a permit. Which method of production has least total cost? cost of production pollution caused ($ per day) (tonnes per day)

The table shows the average incomes of the richest 20% of households and the poorest 20% of households in the UK (2015–2016), and the effects of government taxation and benefits on average income. average income average income (£) of (£) of richest 20% poorest 20% before taxes and benefits 85000 7000 after direct taxes and cash benefits 68000 13000 after all taxes (direct and indirect) and all benefits 63000 17000 What can be concluded from the information in the table?

options.A: The effects of direct taxation have affected the rich less than the poor.
options.B: The government’s policy achieved income equality across households.
options.C: The government redistributed all income taken from the rich to the poor.
options.D: The government’s policy reduced the income inequality between the poor and the rich.

questions.questionText: What would be the most likely effect of the imposition of a national maximum wage below the market equilibrium on the labour market for famous television celebrities?

options.A: a reduction in the number of jobs for television celebrities
options.B: an increase in other methods of rewarding television celebrities
options.C: greater movement of celebrities between television channels
options.D: increased employment of foreign television celebrities

questions.questionText: Which government measure is most likely to encourage faster and more sustainable economic growth in a country?

options.A: subsidies to firms using recycled materials in production
options.B: grants for the exploration and exploitation of new oil deposits
options.C: increased spending on environmental education in schools
options.D: tougher legislative controls on emissions of air and water pollution

questions.questionText: Which statement about National Income accounting is correct when Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is converted into Net National Income (NNI)?

options.A: An allowance for depreciation has to be made, because the NNI does not include output that replaces capital that has been used up.
options.B: Both GDP and NNI have to be calculated by the incomes method, because that is what NNI is measuring.
options.C: Double counting is not a problem if the conversion uses the output method, but it is when using the expenditure method.
options.D: The value of exports needs to be added, because exports generate income for citizens.

questions.questionText: Real GNP per capita is often used when comparisons of living standards are made between a developed and a developing country. What is not a good reason to question the accuracy of this comparison of living standards?

options.A: It is not possible to use price indices accurately when computing real figures because spending patterns are different.
options.B: People in developed countries enjoy very different amounts of leisure time to people in developing countries.
options.C: The extent of the unrecorded economy is very different in the two countries.
options.D: The purchasing power parity theory has been used to make comparisons.

questions.questionText: Based on the International Labour Office definition of unemployment, which individual is most likely to be classified as unemployed?

options.A: a single parent who would like to work but cannot afford to pay for child-care facilities
options.B: a teacher who has decided to retire permanently
options.C: a redundant steel worker who is not actively seeking alternative work
options.D: a student who is desperately seeking any weekend job to supplement his income
